schema_changes: people: categories and visibility. Append to schema.server.ts: `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS categories TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';` and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS directory_visible BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;` and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contact_mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'introduction';` (direct|introduction, checked in app code) and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS share_email BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;` and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS share_phone BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS people_visible_idx ON people (directory_visible, status);`. Existing rows: the column DEFAULTs apply to every existing row (all hidden). A ONE-SHOT backfill guarded by an app_meta key (e.g. 'crm_v2_visibility'), run from bootstrap.server.ts after SCHEMA_SQL and not inside SCHEMA_SQL (which reruns on every boot), sets: `UPDATE people SET directory_visible = TRUE, contact_mode = 'direct', share_email = TRUE, share_phone = TRUE WHERE status IN ('active','new') AND NOT ('funder' = ANY(contribution_types)) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM intake_submissions s WHERE s.person_id = people.id AND s.status = 'new')`. That preserves today's teacher experience for approved partners, hides funders, leads and unreviewed sign-ups, and keeps people with board or staff affiliations visible. The exact rule is an owner decision.

people: categories backfill (same one-shot): `UPDATE people SET categories = ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT c FROM unnest(ARRAY[CASE WHEN 'skills_lesson' = ANY(contribution_types) THEN 'skills_instructor' END, CASE WHEN contribution_types && ARRAY['classroom_volunteer','after_school'] THEN 'volunteer' END, CASE WHEN 'internship' = ANY(contribution_types) THEN 'internship_host' END, CASE WHEN 'cap_partner' = ANY(contribution_types) THEN 'cap_partner' END, CASE WHEN 'funder' = ANY(contribution_types) THEN 'funder' END, CASE WHEN 'other' = ANY(contribution_types) THEN 'other' END, (SELECT CASE o.kind WHEN 'business' THEN 'business' WHEN 'government' THEN 'government' WHEN 'nonprofit' THEN 'community_org' WHEN 'faith' THEN 'community_org' WHEN 'foundation' THEN 'funder' END FROM organizations o WHERE o.id = people.organization_id)]) c WHERE c IS NOT NULL) WHERE categories = '{}';`. contribution_types is left untouched.

people: owner, origin and private vs shareable text. Add `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS owner_user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;` and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin TEXT;` (free text: 'Met at the community reception'; people.source stays as the entry channel) and `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS shared_summary TEXT;` (staff-visible, admin-written) and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS people_owner_idx ON people (owner_user_id);`. Existing people.notes is reinterpreted as private admin notes with no data move. people.funding_focus becomes admin-only. Owner backfill (one-shot, optional): `UPDATE people SET owner_user_id = created_by WHERE owner_user_id IS NULL AND created_by IN (SELECT id FROM users WHERE role = 'admin')`. Others stay NULL (unassigned) unless the owner names a default admin.

people: phone normalisation for duplicate detection. Add `ALTER TABLE people ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS phone_digits TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (right(regexp_replace(coalesce(phone,''), '\D', '', 'g'), 10)) STORED;` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS people_phone_idx ON people (phone_digits) WHERE phone_digits <> '';` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS people_name_org_idx ON people (lower(full_name), organization_id);`. The generated column fills existing rows automatically. PGlite supports generated columns, but verify on both drivers. Do NOT add a UNIQUE index on lower(email) without first checking for existing duplicates: a failing CREATE UNIQUE INDEX in SCHEMA_SQL would stop the server at boot.

people.status vocabulary: keep lead/new/active/inactive as the relationship status. If the owner wants richer values (e.g. 'prospect', 'paused'), add `ALTER TABLE people DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS people_status_check;` and check in app code (PERSON_STATUSES), mirroring the organizations_kind_check precedent. No row changes needed.

opportunities (new): `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS opportunities (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, person_id TEXT REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, organization_id TEXT REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, track TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'engagement' CHECK (track IN ('engagement','funding')), kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'other', title TEXT NOT NULL, stage TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'not_contacted', CHECK ((track = 'engagement' AND stage IN ('not_contacted','contacted','committed','completed','closed_declined','canceled')) OR (track = 'funding' AND stage IN ('identified','cultivating','proposal_submitted','awarded','declined','canceled'))), cap_id TEXT REFERENCES caps(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, owner_user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, expected_on DATE, amount_requested NUMERIC(12,2), amount_awarded NUMERIC(12,2), deadline_on DATE, notes TEXT, closed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_by TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CHECK (person_id IS NOT NULL OR organization_id IS NOT NULL));` plus `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS opportunities_person_idx ON opportunities (person_id);` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS opportunities_open_idx ON opportunities (track, stage, updated_at DESC);`. A staff_request_id column is added in Phase 3. The funding stage names are a proposal for the owner to confirm. No existing rows. Optional one-shot import from cap_partners (see questions): suggested -> not_contacted, contacted -> contacted, confirmed -> committed, declined -> closed_declined, with kind 'cap_partner' and cap_id set.

follow_ups (new): `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS follow_ups (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, person_id TEXT REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, organization_id TEXT REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, opportunity_id TEXT REFERENCES opportunities(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, action TEXT NOT NULL, due_on DATE NOT NULL, owner_user_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open','completed','canceled')), awaiting_response BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, waiting_since DATE, completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, completed_by TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_by TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CHECK (person_id IS NOT NULL OR organization_id IS NOT NULL));` plus `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS follow_ups_open_idx ON follow_ups (status, due_on);` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS follow_ups_owner_idx ON follow_ups (owner_user_id, status, due_on);` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS follow_ups_person_idx ON follow_ups (person_id);`. No existing rows. Optionally seed one open follow-up per current 'lead' person, since the admin overview already lists leads as waiting.

engagements becomes the unified history (preferred over a parallel table, since ActivityTimeline, getCapActivity, the dashboard and AI get_person already read it). Run `ALTER TABLE engagements DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS engagements_kind_check;` with kinds checked in app code (ENGAGEMENT_KINDS widened to: lesson, volunteer, internship, guest_speaker, meeting, call, note, email_sent, email_received, contact_created, signup_submitted, signup_approved, follow_up_scheduled, follow_up_completed, opportunity_updated, engagement_completed, merged). CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS saved_resources (user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, person_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, note TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), PRIMARY KEY (user_id, person_id)). New table.

Engagements, to mark where history came from (place this after staff_requests and email_messages in SCHEMA_SQL): ALTER TABLE engagements ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual' CHECK (origin IN ('manual','staff_request','email','system')); ALTER TABLE engagements ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS staff_request_id TEXT REFERENCES staff_requests(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; ALTER TABLE engagements ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_message_id TEXT REFERENCES email_messages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS engagements_request_person_idx ON engagements (staff_request_id, person_id) WHERE staff_request_id IS NOT NULL; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS engagements_email_idx ON engagements (email_message_id, person_id) WHERE email_message_id IS NOT NULL. Existing rows get origin 'manual' from the default, which is accurate, so existing 'email' rows stay marked as unverified manual logs. New kinds (e.g. 'email_received', 'introduction') would need `ALTER TABLE engagements DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS engagements_kind_check` with app-side checking, the same approach as organizations_kind_check. Coordinate with the Section 7 owner so there is one history table, not two.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_accounts (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provider IN ('google','microsoft')), email_address TEXT NOT NULL, connected_by TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, scopes TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', refresh_token_enc TEXT NOT NULL, key_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, sync_cursor TEXT, last_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','needs_reconnect','disconnected')), last_error TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()); CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS email_accounts_addr_idx ON email_accounts (provider, lower(email_address)). Access tokens stay in memory only and are refreshed per request. Disconnecting deletes refresh_token_enc and revokes the token at the provider.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_messages (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES email_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, provider_message_id TEXT NOT NULL, thread_id TEXT, direction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('sent','received')), from_address TEXT NOT NULL, to_addresses TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', cc_addresses TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', subject TEXT, snippet TEXT, body_text TEXT, sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, sent_via_app BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, sent_by TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE (account_id, provider_message_id)); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_message_people (message_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES email_messages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, person_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, PRIMARY KEY (message_id, person_id)); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS email_message_people_person_idx ON email_message_people (person_id). Recommendation: body_text only for app-sent messages, and snippet/subject only for synced ones (student-data rule).

Optional: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_drafts (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, person_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, author_id TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, purpose TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT, body TEXT, ai_generated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, facts_used JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','sent','discarded')), email_message_id TEXT REFERENCES email_messages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()). This gives an audit of what was AI-drafted and approved by a human. Skip it if client-side drafts are enough.

Ordering note for app/lib/schema.server.ts: SCHEMA_SQL runs top to bottom on every start, so the new CREATE TABLEs (staff_requests, staff_request_people, saved_resources, email_accounts, email_messages, email_message_people) must come before the engagements ALTERs that reference them. All statements must stay idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS) and must work on both PGlite and Neon (no extensions).
risks: Current read leaks for teachers (all server-side, not just the UI): searchPeople() returns email and phone for everyone, including funders, leads and unreviewed 'new' sign-ups (/app/people loader, header search, /app/connections, CAP suggestions, assistant and MCP tools). The /app/people/:id loader sends notes, funding_focus, every engagement with notes and author, all relationships, and peopleOptions (up to 2000 names including funders) to any signed-in user. The app/_index loader sends a 1000-row people table with emails plus everyone's recent engagements. getVillageMap() exposes the whole network. getCapPartners() exposes partner emails.

AI and MCP leaks: the get_person tool (tools.server.ts L286-331) returns notes, relationships and engagement notes for any id, and ToolContext has only userId, so the assistant and every teacher's MCP key (/mcp/<key>) can read private CRM notes and funder data. Text answers containing these details are then saved in assistant_chats, which keeps them even after an admin is demoted to staff.

Inference leak through search: scoring includes notes and funding_focus (searchPeople L121). Even if those fields are hidden, a 'why it matched' line or simply the ranking reveals private note content to staff. Staff search must not score on those fields.

Intro paths reveal hidden people: pathsTo() chains through any person, so a staff member could see 'Rosa (board) knows <hidden funder>, who knows X'. Filter or collapse chains for staff, and favor Request Introduction.

Teacher write paths that pollute admin history or bypass review: on /app/people/:id the intents logEngagement (including kinds email, call, note), addConnection and addToCap are open to teachers. On /app/caps/:id, update-partner and remove-partner lack canEdit. On /app/connections, save-lead lets teachers create people rows (source 'web', status 'lead') outside the sign-up review queue.

OPEN_ACCESS on the live demo makes every anonymous visitor the first admin. Once email exists, that means anyone could send mail as NVA and read synced history. The email routes must refuse in code when OPEN_ACCESS is true, and the real deployment needs a separate database and OAuth client from the public demo. Do not rely on the env being unset.

Visibility defaults: DEFAULT FALSE empties the staff directory on deploy until a backfill or admin approval. DEFAULT TRUE silently exposes funders and leads. Either way the backfill must be an explicit, one-time, app_meta-guarded step that the owner signs off on.

Student data: syncing an admin inbox pulls in messages that may name students (violating 'adults only, never store student data' in AGENTS.md and schema.server.ts). Mitigations: store subject and snippet only, sync only threads with known adult contacts, give admins an exclude/delete control, and do not feed raw bodies to the model beyond the live draft request.

Prompt injection: bios and notes come from public sign-ups, and synced emails come from external senders. Both flow into drafting context. The draft call has no tools (so nothing can be exfiltrated), but injected text can steer the draft, for example by inserting a link. The URL and email post-check plus mandatory human review address this. Never give the drafting model a send tool.

Hallucination with GLM Flash: it may invent dates, amounts or commitments, which matters most for funding follow-ups. Mitigations: numbered facts, placeholders for anything missing, a deterministic post-check that flags unknown numbers, dates, URLs and emails, low temperature, and send only after explicit review. Never auto-send or send on regenerate.

Google OAuth: gmail.send is a sensitive scope, and gmail.readonly (plus compose, modify, metadata) are restricted. With an External consent screen, restricted scopes require Google verification and an annual third-party security assessment (CASA), which takes weeks and costs money. Testing mode issues refresh tokens that expire after 7 days. This is only workable if NVA uses Google Workspace and the app is registered as Internal in NVA's own Cloud project. A consumer @gmail.com admin account cannot use Internal.

Microsoft 365: register a single-tenant app in NVA's Entra ID with delegated Mail.Send, Mail.Read (or Mail.ReadBasic, which leaves out bodies), offline_access, User.Read and openid email. Avoid application permissions, which could read every mailbox in the tenant. The tenant may require admin consent. Client secrets expire (24 months max) and need rotation. Refresh tokens rotate on every refresh, so concurrent serverless requests can race; refresh inside a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on email_accounts and always save the new token.

Token security: losing or rotating EMAIL_TOKEN_KEY without key_version support forces a reconnect. Tokens must never reach logs (the existing console.error calls log error messages, so watch fetch error bodies), the client or the CSV. The OAuth state and PKCE cookie must be signed and short-lived, and the callback must check that the returned account is the expected NVA address.

Deployment constraints: Vercel functions have maxDuration 60s (vercel.json), so sync must be chunked. Vercel Cron frequency depends on the plan (Hobby allows daily). Redirect URIs must be registered exactly for each environment (Vercel URL, Duplo URL from terraform, localhost), and APP_URL is currently only an AI referer. Gmail push (Pub/Sub watch) and Graph change subscriptions need public webhooks and renewal, so defer them and start with on-demand sync.

Gmail history cursors (historyId) go stale after about a week without use, and Graph delta links can expire. Sync needs a fallback to a bounded re-scan, and dedupe on (account_id, provider_message_id) is required.
Microsoft /me/sendMail returns 202 with no message id. To record the sent mail reliably, create the draft (POST /me/messages) and then POST /send, or read the message back from SentItems.

Request completion integrity: double submits or two tabs can log duplicate engagements. Use a guarded status UPDATE plus the partial unique index on (staff_request_id, person_id). logEngagement currently uses the global query outside a transaction and auto-flips people.status to 'active', which may conflict with spec section 5.

Person deletion (deletePerson cascades engagements) silently removes request-linked history and staff_request_people rows. Consider archiving instead of deleting contacts that have requests or emails.

Ownership overlap with other phases: the users.role 'teacher'->'staff' rename (Phase 1), the history/activity model (Section 7), opportunities and follow-ups (Phases 2, 5, 6), and new contribution types such as guest_speaker and mentoring plus a location field (Section 9; search over 'location' is impossible today because people and organizations have no location column). Agree on one design so there are no duplicate history or visibility systems.

i18n burden: every new string needs EN and ES keys (TypeScript enforces this through defineMessages), and AI drafts and reason strings must respect the contact's language. No em dashes, per the repo rule and the owner's memory.
